checks.label: Energy balance (deposited = stored + rejected, from the outputs)
checks.note: largest relative gap over the outputs; threshold 3% of the largest of the energy deposited, rejected and stored so far (the run starts from a steady operating state). Energies are the nominal sphere's (the wedge's divided by 0.999087). The heat made is that of the implicit step (the source at the end of each step, which is how OFFBEAT and the independent solution deposit it; the integral of the table is in the record as "deposited"), and the heat leaving is a trapezoid over the output times, which is poor when the outputs are far apart compared with the time the heat takes to leave: add outputs

checks.label: OFFBEAT vs the independent finite-volume solution (max cell deviation)
checks.note: largest at t = 0.020000000000000014 s; bound 0.172 K = min(3 x 0.062 K [the independent solution's own change when its cells are halved], 0.5% of the peak rise) + 0.02 K

checks.label: Time-stepping error of the peak temperature (step vs half step)
checks.note: the peak changes by at most 0.302 K, at any step of the run, when the step is halved; threshold 2% of the peak rise (0.61 K). If it fails, shorten the time step

checks.label: Temperature limit: kernel, illustrative
checks.note: kernel, illustrative: the hottest kernel cell stays at or below 1200 K (926.85 C). Source: synthetic: an illustrative number chosen for this example, not a design limit or a sourced value. Smallest margin 269.67 K: 930.33 K (657.18 C) at t = 0.0175 s, from the independent solution (every step). This check computes no stress; staying below a limit is not an integrity assessment. It judges cell values: a region's face can be hotter than its hottest cell by up to half a cell's drop, so refine the mesh where a margin is small.
